dissents.topic: Should shard/chunk misalignment raise or warn?

positions.position: warnings.warn is sufficient and is the conventional use of PerformanceWarning across dask; raising breaks existing callers who set array.chunk-size low intentionally and risks regressing pipelines on upgrade.

Silent data loss is worse than a hard failure. Raising forces the user to acknowledge the config conflict before any data is written. The PR author explicitly asked this question; a raise is the right default for a correctness hazard.

dissents.topic: Only checking dw[0] vs all chunk sizes

positions.position: auto chunking with previous_chunks=shard_shape concatenates shards; the first chunk represents the nominal size, and the final remainder chunk is handled safely by zarr's partial-write semantics. Checking dw[0] is sufficient.

If auto chooses non-uniform chunks under tight memory limits, an interior chunk could be misaligned without dw[0] being misaligned. The check should validate every chunk, or at minimum assert regularity.

issues.description: `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` followed by unreachable `break`; raising a Warning subclass as an exception is unidiomatic
issues.detail: Line ~3905 raises `PerformanceWarning`, which is a `Warning` subclass defined as 'A warning given when bad chunking may cause poor performance'. Raising a Warning works but conflates two different semantics (warning vs error), and the trailing `break` is dead code that can never execute. If a hard failure is intended, introduce a dedicated exception (e.g., `ZarrChunkAlignmentError(ValueError)`) or keep `warnings.warn(...)`. The PR description itself flags this as an open question — it should be resolved before merge.

issues.description: Misalignment check uses pre-region chunks, but region branch rechunks to region-adjusted chunks
issues.detail: The new for-loop validates `dask_write_chunks` (the full-array auto-normalized chunks) before the `if region is None` split. In the `else` branch the code then rebuilds `chunks` via `new_blockdim(s, c, r)` and rechunks to those. The check therefore can pass on the full-array chunks while the region-adjusted chunks actually used by `arr.rechunk(chunks)` are misaligned with shards, or vice versa (false positive raise). The check should run on the chunks that will actually be used.

issues.description: Only the first chunk per axis is validated; uneven auto chunks can slip through
issues.detail: `nominal_dask_chunk_size = dw[0]` checks only the nominal chunk size. `normalize_chunks(chunks='auto', previous_chunks=zarr_write_chunks, ...)` typically produces shard-aligned multiples, but under tight `array.chunk-size` it can yield uneven chunkings where interior chunks are smaller than dw[0]. Either iterate every chunk (`all(c % zw == 0 for c in dw[:-1])`) or assert chunk regularity before short-circuiting on dw[0].

issues.description: Error/warning loop break-on-first-axis hides other misaligned axes
issues.detail: Once an axis fails, the loop raises (or breaks). For multi-axis arrays a user may have multiple misaligned axes; reporting only the first leads to whack-a-mole tuning of `array.chunk-size`. Either collect all offending axes into a single message, or recompute the recommended `safe_chunk_size` to satisfy all axes simultaneously (the current `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * itemsize` already does this, but the message names only `axis {ax}` and chunk size `{zw}`, which is misleading when multiple axes are bad).
Python parses this as `not (x % zw == 0)`, which is correct but unidiomatic and easy to misread as `(not x) % zw == 0`. Prefer `if nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0:`.

issues.description: `np.prod(zarr_write_chunks)` returns a numpy scalar in the user-facing message
issues.detail: `safe_chunk_size = np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` yields a numpy int (e.g., `np.int64(12)`), which formats as `np.int64(12)` in the repr-printed dask.config.set example and looks unprofessional. Wrap with `int(...)` before interpolation, or use `math.prod`.

issues.description: Test only verifies `pytest.raises` for the warning path; no remaining coverage for `warnings.warn` semantics
issues.detail: `test_zarr_risky_shards_warns` uses `pytest.raises(PerformanceWarning, ...)`, locking in the raise-on-misalignment behavior. If the team decides to keep this as a warning (per the PR's open question), the test name (`*_warns`) and shape will mislead future readers. The test name and assertion should match the chosen semantics.

issues.description: Parametrized region test does not assert the misalignment path is exercised for region='all' and region='half'
issues.detail: `test_zarr_to_zarr_shards` asserts `c % s == 0` for the resulting chunks across all three region modes, which is good. But it does not assert that the new region-branch code path uses region-adjusted dask_write_chunks correctly when those chunks would have been misaligned at the global level. Add a region test under a constrained `array.chunk-size` to lock in behavior.

issues.description: Error message recommends a chunk-size in bytes but mixes singular ('a single on-disk chunk') with shard semantics
issues.detail: The message says 'set array.chunk-size to at least the size in bytes of a single on-disk chunk (or shard)'. For sharded zarr arrays, `_get_zarr_write_chunks` returns the shard shape, so `safe_chunk_size` is the size of one shard — not the inner chunk. Tighten wording to 'shard' specifically when sharding is active to avoid confusing users into thinking the inner chunk size suffices.

review.summary: The PR correctly improves rechunking by using shard shape as `previous_chunks` so `normalize_chunks(chunks='auto', ...)` typically produces shard-aligned multiples — a real win over #12105. However, the misalignment-detection block has three concrete problems: (1) it `raise`s a Warning subclass and leaves a dead `break`, conflating warning and error semantics on a question the PR description itself flags as unresolved; (2) the check runs on full-array `dask_write_chunks` while the region branch later rechunks to region-adjusted chunks, so the validation and the actual rechunk can diverge; (3) only `dw[0]` is inspected, which is fragile under uneven auto chunkings. The error-message wording and a few stylistic issues (`not x % y == 0`, `np.prod` repr leakage, single-axis report) should be cleaned up. Tests are improved overall but lock in the raise semantics under a `_warns` name, which should be reconciled with whatever decision the team makes on the warn-vs-raise question.
